identity.title: Epigenetic Allostasis in Alcohol Use Disorder: A Metabolic-Chromatin Framework Linking DNA Methylation, Circuit Remodeling, and Precision Therapeutics.

content.abstract: Alcohol Use Disorder (AUD) is a chronic relapsing disorder characterized by persistent dysregulation of reward, stress, and executive circuits. Although acute ethanol effects on neurotransmission are well established, the molecular mechanisms that stabilize long-term vulnerability remain unclear. Building on established allostatic and epigenetic-allostatic models, we develop an expanded framework in which repeated alcohol exposure can drive a transition from adaptive, transient chromatin remodeling toward more persistent epigenetic states across key neural circuits. We integrate evidence from histone modifications, DNA methylation, and metabolic regulation, highlighting how alcohol-induced oxidative stress and disruption of one-carbon metabolism lead to S-adenosylmethionine depletion and methylation instability. These processes converge to form a metabolic-epigenetic trap, reinforcing transcriptional repression of plasticity-related genes. We synthesize circuit-specific changes in the amygdala, prefrontal cortex, nucleus accumbens, and hippocampus, and incorporate emerging human postmortem and single-nucleus multiomic data that support cell-type-specific epigenetic remodeling. In addition, we examine neuroimmune-epigenetic interactions and developmental and sex-dependent exposures as amplifiers of epigenetic vulnerability. Finally, we evaluate therapeutic strategies ranging from selective histone deacetylase inhibition to locus-specific epigenome editing, emphasizing the critical importance of treatment timing and circuit specificity. Together, this expanded framework conceptualizes AUD as a disorder in which maladaptive genomic stability may contribute to persistent circuit dysfunction and identifies epigenetic-metabolic coupling as a testable target for next-generation therapeutics.
